sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:179545
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40670 of 2023

Applicant :- Vishambhar Nath Patel
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Tripathi,Punam Purwar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Vijay Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 197 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Lanka,
District Varanasi during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members including his son i.e.
husband of the deceased and according to the FIR marriage of the deceased was performed with the son of the applicant on 26.05.2017 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for want of motorcycle and when son of the applicant i.e. husband of the deceased came to know that informant sold a land then he demanded Rs. 5 lakhs for doing business and on 25.05.2023 son-in-law of the informant i.e. son of the applicant informed the informant that her daughter had died.

Vishambhar Nath Patel vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51975069/

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is father-in-law of the deceased and only being father-in-law, he has been made accused in the present matter and specific allegation of demand of Rs. 5 lakhs has been made against husband of the deceased in the FIR as well as in the statement of the informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
5.

He next submits that actually some dispute arose between husband and wife and after that deceased committed suicide by hanging herself and this fact is evident from the statement of Umang, the son of the deceased, which has been annexed as Annexure-6 to the affidavit.
6.
He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 25.06.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that applicant is father-in-law of the deceased and there is no specific allegation against him and from the statement of the son of the deceased, it appears that after some dispute between husband and wife deceased hanged herself.
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, daughter-in-law of the applicant died under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home within seven years of her marriage but applicant is father-in-law of the deceased and no specific allegation was made against him and specific allegation of demand of Rs. five lakhs has been made in the FIR and in the statement of the informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
against husband of the deceased.
10.

Further, from the perusal of the statement of Umang, son of the deceased, it appears that after fight between husband and wife, deceased hanged herself and post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant, who is father-in-law, is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant - Vishambhar Nath Patel be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: ( ii )

The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
